metadata.file_name: 4. Zheng et al. (2023). Identifying key features of resilient students in digital reading: Insights from a machine learning approach.pdf
metadata.title: Identifying key features of resilient students in digital reading: Insights from a machine learning approach

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata for seven East Asian economies and constructs an analytic sample by first selecting ESCS-disadvantaged students within each economy and then selecting those with top-quartile digital reading performance across the seven economies. The dependent variable is a binary academic resilience label (ARS vs NRS) derived from ESCS position and reading achievement, and the model uses 105 contextual features scaled using item response theory. The manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights or replicate weights in the SVM training/evaluation, and it instead focuses on ML preprocessing (kNN imputation, normalization, SMOTETomek resampling) and ten-fold cross-validation. Because SVM and the resampling strategy are not described as weight-aware, the analysis should be treated as potentially unweighted with respect to PISA’s complex survey design unless weights are applied in the underlying OECD/PISA database extraction pipeline.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 for seven high-performing Asian economies (B-S-J-Z/CHN, Hong Kong/HKG, Macao/MAC, Taiwan/TWN, Japan/JPN, Korea/KOR, Singapore/SGP). First screened ESCS-disadvantaged students within each economy (bottom 25% of ESCS). Then, within these disadvantaged students, selected those whose digital reading performance was in the top 25% across the seven economies to form the academically resilient group (ARS); the remaining disadvantaged students were labeled non-academically resilient (NRS). Final analytic sample contained 11,496 students (1,397 ARS; 10,099 NRS).

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Digital Reading (15-year-olds), seven East Asian economies
main_findings.target_variable: Academic resilience classification (ARS vs NRS; binary)
main_findings.performance_metrics: SVM (linear kernel) with SVM-RFE and ten-fold cross-validation: Accuracy=87.51%, AUC=94.86%, Recall=95.98%, Precision=83.11%, F-measure=88.63%. Using the optimal top-20 feature subset: Accuracy=84.35%, AUC=92.34%, Recall=91.51%, Precision=80.69%, F-measure=85.42%.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Digital Reading data for ESCS-disadvantaged students across seven East Asian economies, the study leveraged metacognitive strategies (assessing credibility, summarizing, understanding/remembering) and reading enjoyment, alongside ICT resources and teacher feedback, to classify academically resilient (ARS) versus non-academically resilient (NRS) students, finding that a small set of 20 contextual features achieved high discrimination (Accuracy≈84–88%, AUC≈92–95%). This indicates that strengthening digital reading metacognition and sustaining reading enjoyment—while also improving supportive classroom practices and clarifying how students use ICT—may help identify and support resilient learners, though the cross-sectional design and PV1-based labeling prevent causal claims.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2018 digital reading for 11,496 disadvantaged 15-year-olds from seven high-performing Asian economies (CHN, HKG, MAC, TWN, JPN, KOR, SGP). Academic resilience is operationalized as a binary label: students in the bottom 25% of ESCS within their economy who also fall in the top 25% of digital reading performance across the seven economies; the authors use PVREAD1 (first plausible value) as the reading performance indicator. They train a linear-kernel SVM with recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE) on 105 contextual features, after kNN imputation for invalid/missing responses, min–max normalization to [0,1], and SMOTETomek resampling to address class imbalance. In ten-fold cross-validation, the full-feature model reaches Accuracy=87.51% and AUC=94.86%, while the optimal top-20 feature subset yields Accuracy=84.35% and AUC=92.34%. The paper does not report applying PISA sampling/replicate weights, and the cross-sectional PV-based labeling limits causal interpretation of ICT and school-climate effects.
